$comment: Hand-written guidance for agents that cannot be derived from types or TSDoc. Props, descriptions and examples are generated from the source. scripts/build-agent-docs.mjs fails if an export in src/ui/index.ts has no entry here, or the other way around.
$touchTargets: Every interactive control must have a hit area of at least 44px on touch devices (pointer: coarse) and at least 24px otherwise. Use the shared mechanism; never enlarge the visible control for this.
$surfaceComposition: There are five surfaces. Card sits on page, sunken and highlight sit inside card, and modal floats above the page. Table: page = the base; card = content block on the page (cards, panels, table rows); sunken = recessed area inside a card (code, wells, inset fields); highlight = highlighted panel inside a card (a metric, total or goal; dark lighter than the card, light soft gray); modal = floating layer above the page (dialog, menu, select list, popover). Rules: max 3 nested levels; never put a card inside a card (use sunken, highlight or an `hr` hairline instead); highlight sits inside a card, is never nested, and is not for code or inputs (use sunken); modal is never a page background; mark the sunken container with data-surface="sunken" so controls inside use --color-component-on-sunken; controls placed on highlight use --color-component; at rest use a border or a shadow, never both.
$brand: Brand color tokens derive from --color-brand-solid through color-mix: brand-solid-hover, brand-subtle, brand-foreground (75% brand-solid + 25% primary-foreground), brand-foreground-soft and brand-border-default. The focus ring, brand-border-focus, stays text-colored for contrast. Changing --color-brand-solid rebrands the whole family; --color-on-brand-solid-foreground stays white because it is the text on the solid brand surface. Keep brand-foreground at least 4.5:1 on --color-page and --color-card in both themes.
$radius: The radius scale derives from --radius-base (0.5rem), the single source. sm = 0.5x, md = 1x, lg = 1.5x and xl = 2x via calc, so the default scale is 4/8/12/16px. none and full stay fixed. Nested-radius formulas read the same scale.
$motion: Use motion tokens only. Durations stay under 300ms (fast 100, base 160, slow 240). Entrances and user-driven motion use easing-out; exits may use easing-in and the same duration or shorter. Never scale(0): minimum 0.9 (press/tooltip 0.97, popup 0.95, modal 0.96). Never transition: all. Animate only opacity, transform, color, background, box-shadow, plus Accordion and Collapsible height and the Tabs indicator. Anchored popups (Menu, Select, Popover, Tooltip) use transform-origin: var(--transform-origin); Modal stays centered and composes translate(-50%, -50%) with scale. Do not animate theme changes, the focus ring, or list/menu items on hover. prefers-reduced-motion is global: drop scale/transform, keep short fades. Sheet slides from the side with slow/out and follows --drawer-swipe-movement-x. Toast, stagger, scroll-reveal, hold-to-confirm and drag are not implemented; when they exist, keep them under 300ms with easing-out and never scale(0).
$headerHeight: `--header-height` is the height of the sticky site header (3.55rem / 56.8px). The header uses it directly, and `html` uses `scroll-padding-top: calc(var(--header-height) + var(--space-4))` so in-page anchors clear the header.

Text.renders: p (body variants), span (label, caption), code (code); or the element in `as`
Text.composition: `as` accepts only: p, span, label, strong, em, small, div, code. No links or buttons.
Text.whenToUse: Any paragraph, label, caption or inline code that is not a heading. Small styles: `label` for controls (buttons, tabs); `body-sm` for secondary reading text (descriptions, helper text); `caption` for metadata (timestamps, counters, footnotes).
avoid: Headings: use Heading.
Links: use Link.
Actions: use Button.
Setting font-size or color by hand.
Caption size="sm" (10px) for lowercase running text: it is intentional for uppercase metadata, where the extra tracking keeps it legible.
Form labels: use Label, or Field when you also need description and error.
Text.a11y: Do not use tone="subtle" for required text.

Heading.composition: `as` sets the outline level (h1-h6 only); `size` sets only the look.
avoid: Skipping levels (h1 then h3).
More than one h1 per page.
Choosing a level for its look: change `size` instead.
Heading.a11y: Heading order is part of the page structure for screen reader users.

Link.composition: Native anchor props pass through. `href` is required. Put a trailing icon in `endIcon` (no `size`). Set `standalone` for a link used as a standalone action; inline links in a sentence stay inline. For a link styled as a button, use `Button` with `href`.
Link.whenToUse: Navigation to another page, section or resource, inline in text.
avoid: Actions that do not navigate: use Button with onClick.
Links without visible text.
Button-styled navigation: use Button with href.
Link.a11y: Always underlined so it does not rely on color (the underline gets stronger on hover). Use `target="_blank"` only with `rel="noopener noreferrer"`.

Kbd.composition: One Kbd per key; join keys with text such as +.
Kbd.whenToUse: Keyboard shortcuts in docs and UI.
avoid: Using it as a button.
Kbd.a11y: Native kbd semantics. Spell out symbols that screen readers read poorly, for example add VisuallyHidden text.

Badge.renders: span, or the element passed in `render`
Badge.composition: Text children, plus optional `startIcon`/`endIcon` (generated icons, no `size`); never put icons in children. `loading` adds a spinner (`spinnerPosition`: start or end). `variant`: default, inverted, outline, brand, success or danger. Pass `render={<Link href="…" />}` to render a link. Keep text to one or two words; truncate counts to two digits (`99+`).
Badge.whenToUse: Short status or count labels next to other content.
avoid: Using color as the only signal: always include text.
Badges as headings or key indicators: they are secondary and supportive.
Long descriptions: badges are for short labels.
Styling a badge like a button when it acts as one: use Button.
Badge.a11y: Meaning must be in the text; the variant only reinforces it. A badge rendered as a link keeps the link's own accessible name.

Stack.whenToUse: Arranging children in one direction with a consistent gap.
avoid: Two-dimensional layouts: use Grid.
Margins between children: use `gap`.
Stack.a11y: List semantics are restored with role="list" because removing markers drops them in some screen readers.

Grid.composition: `columns` is a number (equal columns), a full grid-template-columns string, or a per-breakpoint object. `minColumnWidth` uses automatic columns and overrides `columns`.
avoid: One-dimensional layouts: use Stack.
Grid.a11y: Visual order should match DOM order.
choosing: Cards, tiles and galleries: use `minColumnWidth` (for example `"16rem"`). Columns fit automatically, with no breakpoints.
Fixed layouts that change by screen (sidebar plus content, 1/2/3 columns): use the responsive `columns` object, for example `{ base: 1, md: 2, lg: 4 }`.
Unequal columns: pass a string such as `"2fr 1fr"`, optionally per breakpoint, for example `{ base: 1, lg: "2fr 1fr" }`.

Container.renders: div (or `as`), centered with a max width
Container.composition: `size` is one of sm, md, lg, xl (container tokens) and limits the content width, not the padding. `padding` uses the spacing scale.
Container.whenToUse: Page-level width limit and side padding.
avoid: Nesting containers.
Full-width sections: put the background on the section and the Container inside it.
Container.a11y: Use `as="main"` once per page for the primary content.

AspectRatio.composition: Reserves space for media before it loads, preventing layout shift (CLS). `ratio` is width divided by height (`16 / 9`, `4 / 3`, `1`) and defaults to 1. Only `div` is rendered; when the media needs a caption, wrap the box in a `figure` yourself. A direct child `img`, `video`, `iframe`, `picture`, `canvas` or `svg` fills the box; images and videos use `object-fit: cover`.
AspectRatio.whenToUse: Images, video, embeds or maps whose size must be reserved before they load, preventing layout shift (CLS).
avoid: Text boxes: the box grows with its content.
Decorative containers with no media.
AspectRatio.a11y: The child needs its own alt text (`img`) or title (`iframe`, `video`); the box adds no semantics.

VisuallyHidden.whenToUse: Text that screen readers must read but sighted users should not see, such as the name of an icon-only button.
avoid: display:none or aria-hidden for this purpose: they remove the content from the accessibility tree.
VisuallyHidden.a11y: Stays in the accessibility tree by design.

Icon.renders: svg on a 256x256 viewBox, filled with currentColor
Icon.composition: Do not pass paths. Import a named icon from the set (CheckIcon, ArrowRightIcon ...) generated by `bun run icons` and listed in /agent/icons.json. Each icon takes `size` (sm 16, md 20, lg 24, xl 32) and `weight` (regular | fill).
Icon.whenToUse: Any glyph. Named icons are decorative by default; pass `label` when the icon is the only carrier of meaning.
avoid: Hand-written <path> children: every icon comes from the generated set.
Meaningful icons without a label.
weight="fill" unless it marks an active or selected state.
Icon.a11y: Without `label` it is aria-hidden. With `label` it is role="img" with that name.

Spinner.renders: span with role="status" containing an svg and VisuallyHidden text, or an aria-hidden span when the label is empty
Spinner.composition: No children. Use `label` to describe what is loading. An empty label makes it decorative and silent.
Spinner.whenToUse: Indeterminate loading of an action or small region.
avoid: Several spinners announcing at once.
Page-level loading of content shape: use Skeleton.
Spinner.a11y: Announces `label` through a status live region; with an empty label it renders no status role, no VisuallyHidden text and aria-hidden="true". Motion follows prefers-reduced-motion.

Skeleton.composition: Shape is text, rect or circle; set width and height with CSS values.
Skeleton.whenToUse: Placeholder for content whose layout is known while it loads.
avoid: Using it as the only loading signal.
Skeleton.a11y: Hidden from assistive technology. Put aria-busy="true" on the container that is loading.

Button.renders: button without `href`; a (or the LinkProvider component) with `href`
Button.composition: `href` decides the element: a Base UI button (`type="button"` by default) or a link from `LinkProvider` that rejects `disabled`, `loading` and `type`. Put icons in `startIcon`/`endIcon` (no `size`). Icon-only needs `startIcon` and one of `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. Sizes: xs 1.5rem/12px icon, sm 1.75rem/16px, md 2.25rem/20px, lg 2.75rem/24px. `pill` uses `--radius-full`; inside ButtonGroup the group's outer-only rounding wins.
Button.whenToUse: An action with onClick (submit, open, confirm, cancel), or navigation that looks like a button with href. Pass `loading` while an action runs.
avoid: Navigation as inline text: use Link.
onClick plus router.push to navigate: use href, or right-click and new-tab semantics are lost.
More than one primary button per view.
Disabling the button to show progress: use `loading`.
Button.a11y: Icon-only controls need `aria-label` (or `aria-labelledby`) and use `startIcon` instead of children; the types enforce it. `loading` sets `aria-busy` and counts as the start slot, and the spinner stays silent so the button's accessible name is the only announcement. With `href` it is a real link (role link), never role button. Keyboard and disabled behavior on the button branch come from Base UI.

ButtonGroup.composition: Pass `orientation` (horizontal or vertical, default horizontal) and one group of related children: `Button`, a `Menu` trigger or an `Input`. Put `ButtonGroupSeparator` between buttons when the shared edge needs a visible division. Give the group an `aria-label` that names the set of actions.
ButtonGroup.whenToUse: Related actions that belong together and read better as one unit, such as Save draft, Preview and Publish.
avoid: Toggling state or choosing between options: use ToggleGroup.
Unrelated actions that do not form a set.
ButtonGroup.a11y: Renders role="group"; recommend an `aria-label` so the group is announced. Each child keeps its own accessible name and focus ring, which stays above its neighbours.

ButtonGroupSeparator.composition: Place between adjacent buttons when the shared edge needs a visible division. `orientation` describes the line: vertical inside a horizontal group (default), horizontal inside a vertical group.
ButtonGroupSeparator.whenToUse: Marking the division between buttons in a ButtonGroup.
avoid: Separating buttons whose shared edge already reads as a division.
Using it as decoration outside a ButtonGroup.
ButtonGroupSeparator.a11y: Exposes role="separator" with an `aria-orientation` that matches the line.

Field.renders: div containing an optional label, the control, a description and an error
Field.composition: Wrap one control: Input, Textarea, Select, Checkbox, RadioGroup, Switch or Slider. `label` is optional: omit it when the control renders its own label or legend (Checkbox, RadioGroup, Switch, Slider). Pass `error`, `required`, `readOnly` and `loading` to Field instead of wiring the control. Controls that carry their own label or legend also accept these props directly.
Field.whenToUse: Every form control, including its validation, required, read-only and loading states.
avoid: A loose red error text below the control: use Field `error`.
Wiring aria-describedby or aria-invalid by hand.
Field.a11y: Base UI wires the label, aria-describedby and aria-invalid; the error is announced politely. `required` sets the native/ARIA required state and prints Required next to the label, or in the control's own label when Field has no label. Errors show after blur or submit, not on the first keystroke (validationMode defaults to onBlur).

Input.composition: Native input props pass through (type, autoComplete, name, required...). Put decorative icons in `startIcon`/`endIcon` (generated icons, no `size`). `loading` replaces the end icon with a spinner. Icons follow the size: sm 16px, md 20px, lg 24px. Inside Field, omit required/readOnly/loading and pass them to Field.
Input.whenToUse: Single-line text entry, read-only values and values that are still loading.
avoid: Using it without Field or aria-label.
Multi-line text: use Textarea.
Hand-wiring validation ARIA: use Field error.
Input.a11y: Needs an accessible name. Set `autoComplete` for personal data fields. readOnly stays focusable and selectable; loading is readOnly with aria-busy=true.

Textarea.composition: Native textarea props pass through; `rows` defaults to 3. Put decorative icons in `startIcon`/`endIcon` (generated icons, no `size`). `loading` replaces the end icon with a spinner. Inside Field, omit required/readOnly/loading and pass them to Field.
Textarea.whenToUse: Multi-line text entry, including read-only and loading values.
avoid: Using it without Field or aria-label.
Hand-wiring validation ARIA: use Field error.
Textarea.a11y: Needs an accessible name. readOnly stays focusable and selectable; loading is readOnly with aria-busy=true.

Checkbox.renders: span role="checkbox" with a hidden native input, inside a label
Checkbox.composition: `label` is required. Use `indeterminate` for a partial parent state. Accepts `error`, `required`, `readOnly` and `loading` directly, or inherits them from Field.
Checkbox.whenToUse: Independent yes/no choices, especially ones submitted with a form.
avoid: Mutually exclusive options: use RadioGroup.
Settings that apply instantly: use Switch.
Checkbox.a11y: The whole label is clickable. Base UI handles keyboard and the mixed state. Invalid uses the danger border and an error linked with aria-describedby; required prints Required; read-only stays focusable and uses the sunken background; loading sets aria-busy and blocks changes.

RadioGroup.renders: fieldset with a legend and a radiogroup
RadioGroup.composition: `legend` is required. Children are Radio elements. Accepts `error`, `required`, `readOnly` and `loading` directly, or inherits them from Field; required prints Required in the legend. Radio is documented under Parts.
RadioGroup.whenToUse: Choosing exactly one option from a short list.
avoid: Long lists: use Select.
RadioGroup.a11y: Arrow keys move the selection. The legend names the group. Invalid uses the danger border and an error linked with aria-describedby; read-only stays focusable and blocks changes; loading sets aria-busy and blocks changes.

Radio.renders: span role="radio" with a hidden native input, inside a label
Radio.composition: Only inside RadioGroup; it is documented under Parts. `value` and `label` are required.
avoid: Using it outside a RadioGroup.

Switch.renders: span role="switch" with a hidden native input, inside a label
Switch.composition: `label` is required. Accepts `error`, `required`, `readOnly` and `loading` directly, or inherits them from Field.
Switch.whenToUse: A setting that turns on or off immediately.
avoid: Choices that need a Save button: use Checkbox.
Switch.a11y: Announced as a switch with on/off state. Invalid uses the danger border and an error linked with aria-describedby; required prints Required; read-only stays focusable and uses the sunken background; loading sets aria-busy and blocks changes.

Select.renders: button role="combobox" with a listbox popup in a portal
Select.composition: Pass `items` ({ value, label, disabled? }), optional `startIcon`/`endIcon` (generated icons, no `size`), and give it `label`, `aria-label` or wrap it in Field. `loading` replaces the end icon with a spinner. Icons follow the trigger size: sm 16px, md 20px, lg 24px. Inside Field, omit required/readOnly/loading and pass them to Field.
Select.whenToUse: Choosing one option from a longer list, including read-only and loading states.
avoid: Two or three options: use RadioGroup.
Free text: use Input.
Hand-wiring validation ARIA: use Field error.
Select.a11y: Keyboard, typeahead and focus come from Base UI. Needs an accessible name. readOnly prevents choosing another option; loading is readOnly with aria-busy=true.

Tooltip.renders: the child element as trigger; a popup div in a portal
Tooltip.composition: `content` is the text. The single child must be focusable and have its own accessible name.
Tooltip.whenToUse: Extra clarity for sighted mouse and keyboard users, such as naming an icon button.
avoid: Essential information: it does not appear on touch and is not linked to the trigger for screen readers.
Interactive content in the tooltip.
Tooltip.a11y: Shows on hover and keyboard focus, hides on Escape. The trigger needs aria-label when it has no text.

TooltipProvider.composition: Place once near the app root. Optional. `delay` (default 600) applies only to the first tooltip; the next ones open instantly.
avoid: Nesting several providers.

Tabs.renders: div with a tablist, tab buttons and tabpanels
Tabs.composition: Pass `items` ({ value, label, content, startIcon?, endIcon?, disabled? }) and an `aria-label`. Icons are generated icons without `size`; tabs are compact and use 16px icons.
Tabs.whenToUse: Switching between related panels in the same place.
avoid: Navigation between pages: use Link.
Hiding content users must read.
Tabs.a11y: Arrow keys move between tabs; roles and aria-controls come from Base UI.

LinkProvider.renders: no element: it provides the link component through context
LinkProvider.composition: Place once near the app root: `<LinkProvider component={NextLink}>`. Link, Button with href, Menu link items, Breadcrumb and Pagination then render with it.
LinkProvider.whenToUse: Making every link in the library use `next/link` (or another router link) from a single place.
avoid: Passing a `render` prop to individual links.
Nesting several providers.
LinkProvider.a11y: No effect on semantics; the provided component must render an `a`.

useLinkComponent.composition: Only needed when building your own link components that should respect LinkProvider. `const LinkEl = useLinkComponent()` returns the provided link component, or `"a"`.
useLinkComponent.whenToUse: Building your own navigation component that should follow LinkProvider.
avoid: Calling it in Server Components: it needs a client component.
useLinkComponent.a11y: The returned component must render an `a`.

Card.renders: div by default; `as` can be article, section or li
Card.composition: `CardHeader` (with `CardTitle`, optional `CardDescription` and `CardAction`) + `CardContent` + `CardFooter`. `size` sets the shared inset through `--card-spacing`; override that variable to use another spacing step. An `img` as the first child is full-bleed with rounded top corners.
Card.whenToUse: Grouping related content in a bordered surface.
avoid: Making the whole card clickable: put a Link inside and keep the card as a container.
Nesting cards: use an `hr` hairline or a sunken region instead.
Card.a11y: A plain container with no role. Use `as="article"` for self-contained content and give it a heading through CardTitle.

CardHeader.composition: Holds `CardTitle`, optional `CardDescription` and `CardAction`. The action aligns with the title at the top end.
CardHeader.whenToUse: The title region of a Card.
avoid: Using it without a CardTitle.
CardHeader.a11y: No role of its own; the heading comes from CardTitle.

CardTitle.renders: h3 by default; `as` sets the heading element
CardTitle.composition: `as` sets the outline level (h2-h6) and `size` sets the look; it defaults to size 6.
avoid: Skipping heading levels to get a smaller look: change `size` instead.
CardTitle.a11y: A real heading, so it appears in the document outline.

CardDescription.whenToUse: Supporting text directly under the card title.
avoid: Long prose: put it in CardContent.

CardAction.composition: Holds a Button (with `href` for navigation) or Badge at the top end of `CardHeader`, aligned with the title.
CardAction.whenToUse: A control that belongs to the whole card.
avoid: Hiding the card title to make room for the action.
CardAction.a11y: Adds no semantics; the control inside needs its own accessible name.

CardContent.composition: The main body between `CardHeader` and `CardFooter`, aligned with both.
avoid: Repeating the header or footer content.

CardFooter.composition: The bottom region for metadata or actions, aligned with the header and content.
CardFooter.whenToUse: Metadata or closing actions at the bottom of a Card.
avoid: Putting the only primary action at the bottom when CardAction would do.

Alert.renders: div with role alert (error, warning) or role status (neutral, info, success)
Alert.composition: Pass `tone` (default `neutral`), an optional `title` and optional content; both can appear alone. Actions (Button, Link or both) go in the content. `startIcon` replaces the tone glyph and `endIcon` adds a trailing icon (no `size`). Icon, title, border and background share one tone color; override `--alert-tone` to change it.
Alert.whenToUse: A message that stays on the page and the user must notice: a general note (neutral), relevant information (info), a completed operation (success), something that needs attention (warning) or a failed operation (error).
avoid: Short-lived confirmations: use Toast.
Using color alone: the tone also changes the icon and you should say it in the text.
Blocking decisions: use Modal role=alertdialog.
Adding visual variants or extra props before a concrete need exists.
Alert.a11y: Announced by screen readers on render. The icon is decorative, and the tone never relies on color alone: the text says what happened.

Avatar.renders: span with role img and the name as aria-label
Avatar.composition: Pass `name` (required), `src` and `size` (`xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg` or `xl`); initials are the fallback. For bots, companies or systems, use `src` with the logo; without it the initials are shown. `status` adds a solid dot at the bottom end with a page-colored ring and appends the state to the name; `badge` with `badgeLabel` adds an avatar badge with an icon inside and appends its label; `outline={false}` removes the avatar border. `status` and `badge` cannot be combined. Every feature scales with `size`.
Avatar.whenToUse: Showing who a person or account is.
avoid: Using it as a button: wrap it in a Button or Link.
Omitting `name`.
Combining `status` and `badge`: they are mutually exclusive.
Avatar.a11y: The name is the accessible name. A status appends the state, and an avatar badge appends `badgeLabel`, such as "Ada Lovelace, online" or "Ada Lovelace, Verified". Initials, status dot and avatar badge are hidden from assistive technology; the status is a plain solid dot whose color is not the only signal, because the state is announced in the accessible name.

AvatarGroup.renders: div role="group" with overlapping Avatar elements
AvatarGroup.composition: Pass `children` (Avatar elements), `max` (default 4) and shared `size` (default md). Avatars overlap by about 25% and each gets a 2px page-colored ring; later avatars stack on top. Avatars beyond `max` collapse into a "+N" item with the component background and label style, labelled "and N more".
AvatarGroup.whenToUse: A compact summary of several people or accounts.
avoid: One avatar: use Avatar directly.
Long lists where every person matters: show them in a list.
AvatarGroup.a11y: The group has role="group"; give it an `aria-label`. Each avatar keeps its own name, and the overflow item is announced as "and N more".

Popover.renders: no element: it only holds the open state (Base UI Popover.Root)
Popover.composition: Structure: Popover > PopoverTrigger + PopoverContent (title required, description optional, PopoverClose).
Popover.whenToUse: Small interactive content tied to a button, such as a form or extra options.
avoid: Plain hints: use Tooltip.
Blocking decisions: use Modal.
Popover.a11y: Focus moves into the popup and Escape closes it. Title is the accessible name.

PopoverTrigger.composition: Child of Popover. Accepts Button props.
PopoverTrigger.whenToUse: The button that opens a Popover.
avoid: Using it outside Popover.
PopoverTrigger.a11y: A real button with aria-expanded and aria-controls.

PopoverContent.renders: div with role dialog in a portal, with a title
PopoverContent.composition: Child of Popover. Requires `title`; `description`, `side` and `align` are optional.
PopoverContent.whenToUse: The panel shown by a Popover.
avoid: Leaving out the title.
PopoverContent.a11y: Labelled by its title. Focus is returned to the trigger on close.

PopoverClose.composition: Inside PopoverContent. Children are the label.
PopoverClose.whenToUse: A button that closes the Popover.
avoid: Icon-only without a label.

Menu.renders: button that opens a role menu with menuitems
Menu.composition: Pass `label` (the button text) and `items`: `{ label, startIcon?, endIcon?, onSelect?, href?, disabled?, destructive? }` or `{ type: "separator" }`. Icons are generated icons without `size`; the trigger follows its button size and menu items are compact (16px).
Menu.whenToUse: A list of actions or links behind one button, such as account actions.
avoid: Navigation between sections of the site: use links.
Form choices: use Select.
Menu.a11y: Arrow keys, Home, End, typeahead and Escape come from Base UI. Items with `href` are real links.

ToastProvider.renders: no visible element until a toast is shown; renders a viewport in a portal
ToastProvider.composition: Place once near the app root, inside Providers. Then call `useToast()` anywhere below it.
avoid: Messages that must stay: use Alert.
Several providers.
ToastProvider.a11y: Live-region announcements, F6 to reach toasts, pause on hover and focus. The dismiss button is labelled.

useToast.composition: `const { show, close } = useToast(); show({ title, description?, tone?, timeout?, startIcon?, endIcon? })`. Icons are generated icons without `size`.
useToast.whenToUse: Showing a toast after an action finishes.
avoid: Calling it outside ToastProvider.
Putting the only copy of important information in a toast.
useToast.a11y: The tone is never the only signal: write it in the title.

Accordion.renders: div with a heading (h3) and button per item and a region per panel
Accordion.composition: Pass `items` ({ value, title, content, startIcon?, endIcon?, disabled? }). Icons are generated icons without `size`. Use `multiple` to allow several open, `disabled` to disable every item and `bordered` for a border around the whole list. To place it inside a Card use `Card` + `CardContent`.
Accordion.whenToUse: Showing long content in short sections, such as FAQs.
avoid: Hiding content users must read.
Navigation between pages.
Accordion.a11y: Each title is a button in a heading with aria-expanded and aria-controls.

Table.renders: table with caption, thead, tbody, th scope and a focusable scroll region
Table.composition: Pass `caption`, `columns` ({ key, header, align? }) and `rows` (objects by key). Use `align: "end"` for numeric columns: they align end and use tabular numbers.
Table.whenToUse: Comparing data across rows and columns.
avoid: Page layout: use Grid or Stack.
Missing caption.
Table.a11y: Real table semantics. The first column is a row header. The scroll wrapper is focusable and named.

Breadcrumb.renders: nav with an ordered list; the last item has aria-current page
Breadcrumb.composition: Pass `items` ({ label, href?, startIcon?, endIcon? }) from root to current page. `separator` defaults to `>` and accepts any node, such as `/` or `·`; it is always hidden from assistive technology. Use `maxItems` (3 or more) to collapse the middle items into an ellipsis menu opened from an icon button labelled Show hidden pages and sized to its content; omit it to show every item. Icons are generated icons without `size`.
Breadcrumb.whenToUse: Hierarchical navigation: showing where a page sits in a site with 3 or more levels.
avoid: Wizards or steps: not a breadcrumb.
Using the current page as a link: it is a span with aria-current="page".
Breadcrumb.a11y: nav > ol; the nav is labelled Breadcrumb by default; the current page is a span with aria-current="page"; separators are hidden from assistive technology; plain links keep keyboard navigation and a visible focus ring.

Pagination.renders: nav with a list of links
Pagination.whenToUse: Moving through content split across URLs.
avoid: Passing a function for the href (it breaks in Server Components).
Infinite lists.
Pagination.a11y: Every page is a link; the current one has aria-current. Previous and Next are removed, not disabled, when unavailable.

Progress.composition: Pass `label` and `value` (number, or null when unknown). Optional `max`.
Progress.whenToUse: Showing how far a task has got.
avoid: Values the user sets: use Slider.
Short unknown waits: use Spinner.
Progress.a11y: role progressbar with aria-valuenow; the label is the accessible name.

Slider.renders: div with one input type range per thumb
Slider.composition: Pass `label` and `defaultValue` (number or [min, max]). Use `thumbLabels` for ranges. Accepts `error`, `required`, `readOnly` and `loading` directly, or inherits them from Field.
Slider.whenToUse: Choosing a number or range by dragging.
avoid: Exact entry: use Input.
A few named options: use Select.
Slider.a11y: Each thumb is a native range input with arrow-key support. The label is the accessible name. Invalid uses the danger border and an error linked with aria-describedby; required prints Required; read-only stays focusable and blocks changes; loading sets aria-busy and blocks changes.

CodeBlock.renders: server component that highlights with Shiki, wrapped around a client view with an icon-only copy button, optional tabs and a focusable region
CodeBlock.composition: Pass `code`, optional `language` and `label`. For alternatives such as package managers pass `tabs` ({ label, code }[]) instead of `code`. Use `highlight={false}` for plain text. Never color code by hand; use CodeBlock.
CodeBlock.whenToUse: Showing code or commands the user will copy.
avoid: Inline code: use Kbd or a code element.
Long documents.
CodeBlock.a11y: The code region is focusable and named; the copy result is announced via role status.

CodeBlockView.renders: client-only presentation of a CodeBlock: tabs, copy button and focusable code region
CodeBlockView.composition: Internal to CodeBlock. Use it only in client components; pass pre-highlighted `html`/`tabHtml` when available, otherwise the code stays plain.
CodeBlockView.whenToUse: Client components that cannot render the server CodeBlock.
avoid: Server pages: use CodeBlock, which highlights automatically.
Coloring tokens by hand.
CodeBlockView.a11y: The code region is focusable and named; the copy result is announced via role status.

Label.callout: For form fields, use Field, which includes built-in label, description, and error handling.
Label.composition: Text children, `htmlFor`, and optional `required` (prints "Required"; the control still needs its own required attribute) and `disabled`. Prefer Field, which wires description, error and ARIA.
Label.whenToUse: A visible label for a custom control composition outside Field.
avoid: Replacing Field for a standard form field.
Using it as a heading or body text.
Relying on an asterisk for required: Label spells out "Required".
Label.a11y: Associate it with the control through `htmlFor`. Required state must also be on the control (native or ARIA).

EmptyState.composition: Pass `title` (required), optional `description`, `icon` (generated icon, no `size`), `action` (usually a Button, with `href` for navigation) and `as` for the heading level (h2-h4, default h3).
EmptyState.whenToUse: A region that has no content yet, with a next step.
avoid: Errors and failures: use Alert.
Loading placeholders: use Skeleton.
Decorating a section that already has content.
EmptyState.a11y: The title is a real heading and carries the meaning; the icon is decorative. Keep the heading level in order with the page.

Sidebar.renders: aside with a nav landmark and a list
Sidebar.composition: Pass `label` (required), `items` ({ label, href?, onSelect?, startIcon?, active?, disabled? }), optional `header` and `footer`. Links render with the LinkProvider component; items without href are buttons.
Sidebar.whenToUse: Primary vertical navigation beside an app's content, especially on desktop.
avoid: Main site navigation in a header: use SiteHeader or links.
More than one primary sidebar on a page.
Using it for unrelated actions: use Menu or a toolbar.
Sidebar.a11y: The nav landmark is named by `label`; the active item gets aria-current="page". Disabled items are not focusable links and are not clickable.

Collapsible.renders: div with a button trigger and a region panel
Collapsible.composition: Pass `title`, panel `children`, optional `startIcon`/`endIcon` (generated icons, no `size`), open state (`defaultOpen`, `open`, `onOpenChange`) and `disabled`.
Collapsible.whenToUse: A single section that expands, such as advanced options or extra details.
avoid: A set of sections: use Accordion.
Hiding critical content users must read.
Navigation between pages.
Collapsible.a11y: The trigger is a button with aria-expanded and aria-controls; the panel is its region. Keyboard behavior comes from Base UI.

ToggleGroup.composition: Pass `label` (required accessible name), `items` ({ value, label, startIcon?, disabled? }), optional controlled value, `size` (sm or md) and `disabled`. Single choice only.
ToggleGroup.whenToUse: Two to five short, mutually exclusive options, such as a view switch.
avoid: Long content changes: use Tabs.
Independent on/off choices: use Checkbox or Switch.
More than five options: use Select.
Related actions that are not a choice: use ButtonGroup.
ToggleGroup.a11y: Arrow keys move between toggles and roles come from Base UI. The group needs its `label`; selected state is exposed with aria-pressed.

ScrollArea.renders: div frame with a focusable scroll viewport and custom scrollbars
ScrollArea.composition: Pass `children`, optional `label` (accessible name of the scroll region) and `className` to set the height. Default maximum block size is 12rem; override it with a layout class.
ScrollArea.whenToUse: A fixed-height list, code area or panel that should scroll inside the page.
avoid: The whole page scrolling: let the page scroll.
Overflowing menus and popups: they handle it themselves.
Horizontal-only swipe carousels with no keyboard alternative.
ScrollArea.a11y: The viewport is keyboard focusable and shows a focus ring, so keyboard users can scroll it. Give it `label` when the content is not self-explanatory.

Sheet.renders: a trigger button; when open, a backdrop and a side panel in a portal
Sheet.composition: Pass `trigger` (button text), `title`, optional `description`, `children`, `footer`, `side` (left or right, default right) and open state. One component, no parts.
Sheet.whenToUse: Secondary tasks, settings and filters that slide in from an edge.
avoid: A centered decision: use Modal.
Non-essential information: use Tooltip or inline content.
Sheets without a title.
Sheet.a11y: Focus is trapped and returned, Escape closes, the page behind is inert, and the title names the sheet. The close button has an accessible label.

Combobox.renders: input role="combobox" with a filterable listbox popup
Combobox.composition: Pass `items` ({ value, label, description?, startIcon?, disabled? }), a `label` or `aria-label`, and optional `placeholder`, `emptyMessage`, `startIcon`, `size` (sm, md, lg) and open/selection state. Inside Field, omit required/readOnly/loading and pass them to Field. Icons are generated icons without `size`.
Combobox.whenToUse: Choosing one option from a long list when typing to filter helps.
avoid: Fewer than about seven options: use Select.
Several choices: use Checkbox or a multi-select pattern.
Free text that is not from the list: use Input.
Combobox.a11y: Filtering, keyboard navigation and focus come from Base UI. Needs an accessible name from `label`, `aria-label` or Field. The popup is announced with the result count.

Modal.renders: no element: it holds the open state and provides the role (Base UI Dialog.Root, or AlertDialog.Root for role=alertdialog)
Modal.composition: Structure: Modal > ModalTrigger + ModalContent (title, optional tagline/icon/description, body children, actions). Put one to three actions in `actions`: the safe action first and the primary action last. The form lives in the body; a submit button in the footer targets it with the `form` attribute.
Modal.whenToUse: Interrupting the user for a decision or a focused task.
avoid: Non-essential information: use inline content, Alert or Tooltip.
Short-lived confirmations: use Toast.
Modals without a title.
choosing: Content and forms: Modal with the default role="dialog".
A decision that interrupts: Modal role="alertdialog"; add color="critical" for a destructive action.
Blocking information that needs no form: Modal role="alertdialog".
Modal.a11y: The title is the accessible name and the description is the accessible description. Focus is trapped and returned, Escape closes unless dismissible is false, and the page behind is inert. Alert dialogs require a description and start focus on the safe action.

ModalTrigger.composition: Direct child of Modal. Accepts Button `variant` and `size`; use `danger` for the destructive trigger.
ModalTrigger.whenToUse: The button that opens the modal.
avoid: Using a plain Button to open it.
ModalTrigger.a11y: Gets aria-haspopup and expanded state from Base UI.

ModalContent.renders: div role="dialog" (or role="alertdialog" from the root) in a portal, plus a backdrop
ModalContent.composition: `title` is required and children are the body. `description`, `tagline`, `icon`, `actions` and `closeLabel` are optional. The body scrolls while the header and footer stay visible. Actions stack on mobile with the primary on top.
avoid: Omitting `title`.
Putting the form in the footer instead of the body.
More than three actions.
ModalContent.a11y: The title is the accessible name; the description is the accessible description. A dialog focuses the first field when the body has a form; an alert dialog focuses the safe action.

ModalClose.composition: Inside ModalContent `actions`. Accepts Button `variant` and `size`; use `danger` for the destructive action. Mark the safe action with `initialFocus` in an alert dialog.
avoid: Closing by custom onClick state when ModalClose is enough.
ModalClose.a11y: Closing returns focus to the trigger, or to returnFocusTo when the trigger no longer exists.
